title: People judge themselves in control of movements they did not control

statements.text: Wegner and others describe participants who judged themselves to have partial control of movements they in fact did not control, and Nisbett and Wilson showed that people give reasons for judgments that are not their actual causes. So a sense of control is not evidence that conscious intentions affect nonlinguistic behavior. These results do not show consciousness inefficacious, and do not address whether experiences cause reports of them.
